en: One client's books: journal, ledger, bank matching, month-end close
The books of one client business, from journal to month-end close
every line sits in an entry with its account, month and source, and the sheet flags any entry where debits do not equal credits
General ledger by account and month
opening balance, debits, credits and closing balance for every account and month, added up from the journal with no typing
Trial balance that proves the books
debit and credit balances for every account with a check that both sides agree, shown on the dashboard
Bank lines with matching and rule suggestions
each statement line gets a status of matched, not yet booked or needs a category, and a rule suggests the account from the payee
Reconciliation that proves the difference is zero
statement balance, deposits in transit, uncleared payments and unbooked bank items give an adjusted bank and adjusted books with the difference for each month
Ageing that agrees with the ledger
customer invoices and supplier bills sit in ageing buckets, and control checks compare them with the ledger accounts
Expense claims with missing receipt flags
claims above your receipt limit with no receipt are flagged, with the days waiting and an approval check
Accruals and prepayments spread over the months
each item shows the months used, the amount charged to expenses and what is still carried on the balance sheet
purchases, usage and losses give the quantity on hand, the average cost, the stock value and a reorder flag
Fixed assets with depreciation and net book value
cost, life and end value give the depreciation each month, the amount so far and the net book value
nine close tasks for each month, the share done, the status and a check that the month's debits equal its credits
drawings, dividends and capital added with a running total, so the owner sees what was taken from the business

The list of accounts this business uses, with its normal side. Lines, debits, credits, balance and last posting come from the Journal, so you see which accounts are live.
Journal entries (one row for each debit or credit line)
Every posting in the books: one row for each line, grouped by entry number. The account name, month and whether the entry balances come out by themselves, so a wrong entry shows red.
General ledger: each account by month
One row for each account and month: opening balance, debits, credits, movement and closing balance, all added up from the Journal. Debit balances are positive and credit balances negative.
One row for each account: debits, credits and the balance on its side. The two balance columns must add up to the same figure; the dashboard check says if they do not.
Every bank statement line: money in or out, the account you book it to and the journal entry it matches. Status shows what is matched, not yet booked or without a category.
One row for each month end: statement balance, deposits and payments in transit and bank items not yet booked. The book balance and the difference, which must be zero, fill in by themselves.
One row for each payee or payer you see often and the account it goes to. The Bank Statement Lines sheet suggests this account; uses, total and last date are counted from the bank lines.
Customer invoices (money owed to the business)
Every sale on credit: tax, total, balance, due date, days overdue, ageing bucket and status come out by themselves from the amount paid and the terms.
Every purchase on credit: tax, total, balance, due date, days overdue and status, so you pay on time and see what the business owes each supplier.
What customers owe and what the business owes, in each ageing bucket, counted from the invoices and bills. Use it to chase the oldest customer balances and to plan which bills to pay first.
Every payment from the cash box and every top-up. The running balance, the missing receipts above your limit and the account each purchase goes to are worked out for you.
Money staff spent for the business. Each claim needs a receipt above your limit; the status shows what is ready to pay, what is missing a receipt and how many days a claim has waited.
Costs paid ahead (prepayments) or owed but not yet billed (accruals), spread over the months they belong to. Months used, amount charged and what is still carried are calculated.
Stock on hand by item (weighted average cost)
One row for each stock item: opening quantity, what was bought and used, quantity on hand, the weighted average cost and the value. A flag shows what to reorder.
Every purchase, use and loss of stock. Purchases carry their own unit cost; everything else is valued at the item's weighted average cost, so the stock value stays right.
Money the owner takes out or puts in. It shows the effect on equity, a running total and the month, so the owner sees what was taken against the profit.
Each purchase of equipment: cost, life, depreciation each year and month, the months used, depreciation so far and the net book value. It follows the same rule as the monthly journal entry.
Money moved between the business's own accounts, such as cash banked or a top-up of the cash box. The sheet checks the journal and says if the transfer is posted.
One row for each month with a tick for every close task. The share done, the status and the check that the month's debits equal its credits come out by themselves.
The balance of every account on the first day of the books. Debits must equal credits; the difference and the account name fill in by themselves.

Hi {claimant}, your claim {claim_id} for {descr} ({amount}) has no receipt yet. Please send a photo of it so we can pay and book it.
Hi {claimant}, a reminder: claim {claim_id} has waited {days_open} days for a receipt. Please send it this week.
Hi {claimant}, claim {claim_id} for {amount} is complete and will be paid in the next payment run.
Hi {claimant}, we paid claim {claim_id} of {amount} on {paid_on}. Thank you for sending the receipt.
Hi {claimant}, claim {claim_id} for {amount} is above the approval limit, so the owner needs to approve it before we pay.
Hello {customer}, invoice {inv_no} for {amount} is ready. It is due on {due}. Thank you.
Hello {customer}, a reminder that invoice {inv_no} for {balance} is due on {due}.
Hello {customer}, invoice {inv_no} is {age} days overdue. The balance is {balance}. Could you pay it this week?
Hello {customer}, thank you for your payment on invoice {inv_no}. The balance left is {balance}.
Hello {customer}, we received payment of invoice {inv_no}. Thank you, it was a pleasure to serve you.
Hello {supplier}, bill {bill_no} for {balance} is due on {due}. We will pay it on time.
Hello {supplier}, we paid {paid} against bill {bill_no} on {paid_on}. Please confirm you have received it.
Hello {supplier}, we have a question about bill {bill_no} for {amount}. Could you send the delivery note?
Hello {supplier}, bill {bill_no} is {age} days overdue. We are sorry and will pay {balance} shortly.
Hi, the bank shows {descr} with {payee} on {date}. What was it for? We need it to match the books.
Hi, we see money in of {deposit} on {date} from {payee}. Which customer or invoice is it?
Hi, may we book the bank line {line_id} ({payee}) to {suggest}? Please confirm or tell us the right account.
Hi, the bank reconciliation for {month} is done. Difference: {diff}. Result: {state}.
Hi, the reconciliation for {month} shows a difference of {diff} and {unmatched} unmatched lines. Can you check the statement for us?
Hi, we have started the month-end close for {month}. {done} of 9 tasks are done so far.
Hi, the books for {month} are closed. Your figures are ready for review.
Hi, we cannot close {month} yet. Only {done} of 9 tasks are done. Please send what is missing.
Hi {custodian}, the petty cash box shows {balance} after voucher {pv_id}. Please plan a top-up.
Hi {custodian}, voucher {pv_id} for {cash_out} has no receipt. Please find it before the month end.
Hello {supplier}, please send your final bill for {descr}. We have set aside {carried} so far.
Hello {supplier}, please send the invoice and warranty for {descr} bought on {date}. We need them for the asset register.
Hi, we recorded {amount} on {date} as {kind}. The net taken so far is {running}.
Hello {supplier}, we have {on_hand} {unit} of {item} left and need to order more. What is your next delivery date?
Sample wording: adapt it to your country's law and your own practice.
Missing receipt request from {set:firm} for {set:business}, sent on {today}.
Dear {col:claims.claimant}, expense claim {col:claims.claim_id} of {col:claims.amount} for {col:claims.descr}, spent on {col:claims.date}, has no receipt.
The claim has been waiting {col:claims.days_open} days. Spending above {set:receipt_limit} needs a receipt or an invoice so that the cost and the tax on it can be booked and claimed.
Please send a photo of the receipt, or write to us if it is lost so we can note what happened. We cannot pay or book the claim until we have one of the two.
Bank reconciliation for {set:business}, month starting {col:recon.month}. Prepared by {set:firm}.

The bank statement balance is {col:recon.stmt_bal}. Deposits not yet on the statement are {col:recon.transit} and payments not yet cleared are {col:recon.outstanding}. The adjusted bank balance is {col:recon.adj_bank}.
The balance in the books is {col:recon.book}. Bank items not yet booked are {col:recon.unposted}. The adjusted book balance is {col:recon.adj_book}.
The difference between the two is {col:recon.diff}. Result: {col:recon.state}. Lines not yet matched this month: {col:recon.unmatched}.
By signing below, the preparer confirms the figures above agree with the bank statement and the books, and the reviewer confirms any difference has been explained.
Month-end close for {set:business}, month starting {col:close.month}. Prepared by {set:firm}.
{col:close.done} of 9 close tasks are complete. Status: {col:close.state}. The debits less credits for the month are {col:close.diff}, which must be zero.
Tasks covered: bank reconciliation, receivables and payables review, accruals and prepayments, depreciation, stock count, petty cash count, sales tax or VAT check, payroll and the trial balance.
Once signed, entries dated in this month are locked. Any later change needs a dated adjusting entry in the open month with a short reason.
Year-end handover note to the accountant
Year-end handover note for {set:business}, from the books kept by {set:firm}. Month reference: {col:close.month}.
The books are ready for the annual accounts when the last month is closed. This month shows {col:close.done} of 9 tasks done and a debit less credit difference of {col:close.diff}.

With this note we hand over: the trial balance, the general ledger, the bank reconciliations, the receivables and payables ageing, the fixed asset register with depreciation, the stock count, the accruals and prepayments schedule and the owner drawings.
Please list any adjustment you want us to post, and tell us which accounts you would like to review first.
Payment reminder from {set:business} to {col:invoices.customer}, sent on {today}.

Invoice {col:invoices.inv_no} of {col:invoices.amount}, issued on {col:invoices.issued}, was due on {col:invoices.due}. We have received {col:invoices.paid} and the balance of {col:invoices.balance} is {col:invoices.age} days overdue.
If you have already paid, please ignore this note and send us the payment date. If not, please pay by bank transfer and quote the invoice number.
If anything on the invoice is wrong, tell us and we will correct it.
Bill {col:bills.bill_no}, received on {col:bills.received}, has a total of {col:bills.amount}. It was due on {col:bills.due}.
We have paid {col:bills.paid} so far. The balance still open is {col:bills.balance}.
Please check that this agrees with your statement and tell us at once if it does not.
The bank statement shows a line on {col:bank.date}: {col:bank.descr}, from or to {col:bank.payee}. Money in is {col:bank.deposit} and money out is {col:bank.withdrawal}.
We cannot match it to an invoice, a bill or a journal entry yet. Current status: {col:bank.status}.
Please tell us what it was for and send any document that goes with it. Until then we will hold it in a suspense account.
Fixed asset note for {set:business}, prepared by {set:firm}.

{col:fixed.descr} was bought on {col:fixed.date} from {col:fixed.supplier} for {col:fixed.cost}. It is treated as equipment and depreciated over {col:fixed.life} years to a value of {col:fixed.salvage} at the end.
Depreciation is {col:fixed.monthly} a month. After {col:fixed.used} months the depreciation so far is {col:fixed.accum} and the net book value is {col:fixed.nbv}.
Please keep the supplier invoice and the warranty with this note.
Owner money statement for {set:business}, prepared by {set:firm} on {today}.
On {col:drawings.date} an amount of {col:drawings.amount} was recorded as {col:drawings.kind}, paid by {col:drawings.method}. Note: {col:drawings.note}.
The net amount taken out up to and including this date is {col:drawings.running}. This is a movement in equity, not a business expense.
Please confirm that this is correct. Keep in mind that taking out more than the profit reduces the capital of the business.
Adjustment memo for {set:business}, prepared by {set:firm} on {today}.
Months used: {col:accruals.elapsed}. Charged to expenses so far: {col:accruals.recognised}. Still to charge: {col:accruals.remaining}. Carried on the balance sheet: {col:accruals.carried}.

Open Start and type your practice name, the client business and your rules in the yellow cells: tax rate, bank opening balance, receipt limit, bank difference you accept and your targets.
Use one copy of this workbook for each client business. The demo shows a restaurant so you can see every page working; clear the demo rows before you start a real client.
Check Chart of Accounts: one row for each account with its type. Add or rename accounts to fit the client; balances come from the Journal.
Fill Opening Balances with the balance of every account on the first day. Debits must equal credits; the difference shows by itself.
Post every transaction on Journal Entries: one row for each debit or credit line, with the same entry number on each line of an entry. The sheet flags any entry that does not balance.
Read General Ledger and Trial Balance each month. The ledger shows each account by month, and the trial balance proves the debits equal the credits.
Enter every bank line on Bank Statement Lines with the matching entry number. Add rules on Categorisation Rules so repeat payees get the same account each time.
Reconcile each month on Bank Reconciliation: type the statement balance and the reconciling items; the difference must be zero or explained.

Record credit sales on Customer Invoices and credit purchases on Supplier Bills with the amounts paid. Ageing shows what to chase and what to pay first, and control checks compare them with the ledger.
Use Petty Cash, Receipts and Expense Claims to track small spending, missing receipts and what staff are waiting to be paid.
Spread costs over time on Accruals and Prepayments, track stock on Inventory Movements and Stock Summary, and keep equipment on Fixed Asset Additions.
Keep Owner Drawings and Transfers Between Accounts up to date so owner money and moves between accounts are never booked as expenses.
Tick each task on Month-End Close; the checklist turns the steps into dates. Close a month only when it shows 9 of 9 and the debits less credits are zero.

Use the 14 calculators for reconciliation differences, accruals, prepayments, petty cash counts, margins, cash runway, owner pay, expense splits, currency revaluation, stock valuation, loan interest, tax conversion and break-even.

Print vouchers, claim forms, reconciliation statements, ledger cards and letters from the printable sheets by choosing the number in the yellow cell, and tap a message link to open WhatsApp with the text already written.

Read Books Dashboard and Charts each week: bank, profit, what is owed, what is owing, control checks and unfinished month-end tasks at a glance. This workbook helps you keep books and is not tax or legal advice.
Tax deadlines, returns, notices and penalties for every client in one file
sales tax or VAT, income tax, payroll, withholding and annual accounts for all clients over 12 months, with days to go and a status
Filing tracker from first request to accepted
each return moves through seven stages with hours, fee and preparer, so you see which returns are stuck before the deadline
tax charged and tax on purchases give the tax to pay or refund, the due date and a check that the detail lines add up to the return
Income tax estimate by bands or company rate
profit, add-backs and reliefs give the taxable profit and the tax for each business type, the instalments paid, the balance and the monthly amount to set aside
Instalments and prepayments with days late
every instalment shows the amount left, days late and a status, so a missed prepayment is seen before interest builds up
the gross payment and rate give the tax withheld, the net paid and the date to remit, with overdue remittances flagged
flat penalty, percentage penalty and interest are added up and the cause says whether the client or the practice bears the cost
Tax notices and audits with reply dates
each letter from an authority has a reply date, days left and a status, and each audit shows hours spent and the tax at risk
Deductions review with a business share
each expense gets a business share and a decision; the deductible part, the part disallowed and the tax saved come out using your own meal and rate settings
losses show the balance left, the last year to use them and their tax value; assets show claims so far and the tax written-down value
company tax, tax on pay and take-home are worked out for each owner and compared with the best split
Return documents chased by days waiting
every document asked for is timed from the request, so a client holding up a return is marked chase now

One row for each client with country, business type, registration and turnover; open returns, overdue deadlines, next due date, tax paid and penalties fill in from other sheets.
Registered for sales tax or VAT
Every return and payment date for every client over 12 months. Type the date filed and the status shows filed, filed late, overdue or due soon.
Filing tracker: where every return stands
One row for each return being prepared: stage from not started to accepted, hours, fee and who prepares it. The status shows whether it is filed on time, late, overdue or due soon.
Sales tax or VAT returns by period
One row for each client return: sales, tax charged and tax paid on purchases. The tax to pay or refund, the due date and the status fill in, and the detail lines are checked against the totals.
Sales tax or VAT lines on sales and purchases
The invoice and bill lines behind a return: type the net amount and the tax rate and the tax, the gross amount and the month come out. Use it to prove the totals on the return.
Income tax estimate for every client
One row for each client and tax year: profit, add-backs and reliefs give the taxable profit and the tax by bands for individuals or at the company rate. The instalments paid give the balance left.
Each instalment of each client: due date, amount, paid and when. Days late, the amount left and the status (paid, part paid, overdue or upcoming) fill in by themselves.
Withholding tax on payments to others
Each payment from a client to a supplier, landlord or lender that needs tax withheld: type the gross amount and the rate; the tax withheld, the net paid, the remit date and the status come out.
Every penalty or interest charge with its cause. Type the unpaid tax and the days late; the flat penalty, the percentage penalty, the interest and the total come out, and who bears the cost.
Each request for more time: the original date, when you asked, the new date and the answer. It shows the days gained and whether you asked before the deadline.
Each letter from an authority: type, amount, the reply date and when you replied. The days left and the status (answered, waiting, due soon or overdue) fill in so no notice is missed.
Each payment to an authority for a client with the kind of tax, method and bank reference. It feeds the tax paid on every client and the cash plan by month.
Each expense you check before a return: type the amount, business share and decision; the deductible part, the part disallowed and the tax saved come out.
Each asset with cost, purchase date and the yearly allowance rate. The years held, the allowance claimed so far, the tax written-down value and this year's claim come out.
Each tax loss with the year it arose and how much has been used. The balance left, the last year it can be used and its tax value fill in, so no loss expires unnoticed.
Salary and dividend planner for company owners
Each company owner: the profit before pay, the salary and the dividend planned. It works out the company tax, the tax on each, the take-home pay and whether another split would leave more.
Annual returns, ownership updates, accounts filings and licence renewals due at business registries. Type the date filed and the status shows on time, late, overdue or due soon.
Each document you ask a client for before a return: when asked and when received. The days waiting and the status (received, waiting or chase now) show which clients are holding up the work.
Audit and information requests from authorities
Each audit or information request: scope, reply date, hours spent and the outcome. It shows the status, the days open and the extra tax at risk from any adjustment.

Open Start and type your practice name and your rates in the yellow cells: sales tax or VAT rate and days to file, penalty and interest rates, income tax bands, company rate, loss years and warning days.

Tax rates and penalty rules differ by country. Every rate in this workbook is your own setting, so check them against the rules where each client is taxed: the workbook tracks your work and is not tax or legal advice.

Fill Client Tax Profiles: one row for each client with country, business type, registration, turnover and year-end month. Open returns, overdue deadlines, tax paid and penalties fill in by themselves.
Use Deadline Calendar as your master list: one row for each return or payment date. Type the date you filed and the status changes to filed, filed late, overdue or due soon.
Track the work on Filing Tracker: move each return through the stages from not started to accepted, and fill in hours and fee to see the fee per hour.
Enter each sales tax or VAT return on Sales Tax or VAT Returns, and the invoice and bill lines on Tax Lines. The sheet checks that the lines match the tax charged on the return.

On Income Tax Estimates enter profit, add-backs and reliefs for each client. The tax follows your bands or company rate, and the instalments paid on Tax Instalments give the balance and the monthly set-aside.
Record every payment to an authority on Tax Payments and every payment that needs tax withheld on Withholding Tax. The remit date and status come out by themselves.
Log every penalty with its cause on Penalties and Interest, so you see how much the practice paid itself, and every request for more time on Extension Requests.
Log each letter from an authority on Tax Notices and each audit on Audit Requests with the reply date. Overdue replies show in red on the dashboard.
Review expenses on Deductions Review, assets on Tax Depreciation, losses on Loss Carry-Forward and owner pay on Pay and Dividend Planner before the year ends.
Ask clients for records on Return Documents. Anything waiting more than twice your warning days shows as chase now.
Use the 14 calculators to check a return, estimate income tax by bands, plan instalments, price a penalty, plan a loss, compare salary and dividend, and set aside tax each month.

Print client tax cards, return sheets, notice files and certificates from the printable sheets, choose letters and checklists by the number in the yellow cell, and tap a message link to open WhatsApp with the text ready.
Read Tax Dashboard and Charts every week: deadlines, overdue returns, tax still to pay, penalties, open notices and documents to chase at a glance.
